text: What was the Language Movement of 1952? It was a mass movement in East Pakistan demanding Bangla as a state language, culminating in police firing on protesters in Dhaka on 21 February 1952.
Why did students protest in February 1952? They opposed the Urdu-only state-language policy and demanded constitutional recognition of Bangla in state and public life.
Who were the key martyrs of 21 February? Abul Barkat, Abdul Jabbar, Rafiq Uddin Ahmed, Abdus Salam, and others are remembered as central martyrs of the movement.
Why is 1952 important beyond language policy? It transformed cultural rights into political consciousness and became a foundational step toward later autonomy and independence struggles.
In 1952, the right to speak Bangla became the right to exist with dignity.
source: Historical reflection on the Language Movement
